title: Finite presentation is closed under kernels, images, and cokernels over a coherent ring
statement: Let R be a commutative ring such that every finitely generated ideal of R is finitely presented. If f:M\to N is an R-linear map between finitely presented R-modules [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], then \operatorname{Ker}(f), \operatorname{Im}(f), and \operatorname{Coker}(f) are finitely presented R-modules [def-sc-finitely-presented-module].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 05CW (coherent modules form an abelian category), together with Lemma 05CX (over a coherent ring, coherent modules are exactly finitely presented modules)

proof.text: Coherent here means (Stacks Definition 05CU) finitely generated with every finitely generated submodule finitely presented; the hypothesis says exactly that R is coherent as a module over itself. By Stacks Lemma 05CW(4) and induction on n, R^n is coherent; a finitely presented module is the cokernel of a map R^a\to R^b, hence coherent by 05CW(3) (this is the argument of Stacks Lemma 05CX). So M and N are coherent. By 05CW(2) applied to f:M\to N (M finite, N coherent), K=\operatorname{Ker}(f) is finitely generated; as a finitely generated submodule of the coherent module M it is finitely presented by Definition 05CU.

Choose finite generators m_1,\ldots,m_r of M. Their images f(m_i) generate I=\operatorname{Im}(f), so I is finitely generated. As a finitely generated submodule of the coherent module N (step 1), I is finitely presented by Stacks Definition 05CU (equivalently 05CW(1)).

The cokernel is N/I. Take a finite presentation R^a\to R^b\to N\to0 and finite generators i_1,\ldots,i_s of I (step 2). Lift the i_j to R^b and append these lifts to the finitely many relation generators for N; the resulting finite presentation presents N/I. Thus \operatorname{Coker}(f) is finitely presented.
